fields.v: Academia: Beihang University (State Key Laboratory of Complex & Critical Software Environment), China; The University of Hong Kong
Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — CodeSpec (dual executable specifications) compared with five coding-agent scaffolds on FeatureBench and NL2Repo-Bench, with ablations

CodeSpec (authors'; code at github.com/zhu-zhu-ding/CodeSpec), no version. Baselines: OpenHands, Mini-SWE-Agent, Claude Code, Codex, RTADev (architecture-first, textual designs); versions not stated. Variant: CodeSpec (Text) with textual instead of executable specs

Sub-requirements decomposed from the feature instruction; evidence-grounded functional chain per sub-requirement (units linked by evidence pairing requirement semantics with repository design patterns, call relations, dependencies); executable architecture specification per chain (CheckUnit, CheckRelation, CheckDataFlow); executable behaviour specification per chain (CheckOutput, CheckBoundary, CheckState, pytest-style)

(1) Functional chain construction: decompose instruction into sub-requirements, identify candidate units, evidence-driven chain reasoning; (2) dual executable specification compilation (architecture spec from template, then behaviour spec); (3) specification-guided code generation loop (Algorithm 1): edit patch -> execute architecture and behaviour checks -> revise until all pass or interaction budget K exhausted. Greenfield (NL2Repo): first create repository skeleton and units
None (fully automated)
Full workflow (plus ablations removing each specification type and the evidence grounding)

Not stated in Böckeler terms. Executable specifications generated per feature and enforced throughout implementation to keep 'design-implementation consistency'; not maintained after the task (closest to spec-first, draft)
fields.why: Executable specifications are generated per feature before coding and enforced by execution throughout the loop (Algorithm 1, p. 4), which a reader could call spec-anchored for the task's duration; they are not kept after the task, so spec-first remains the best value

Criterion: benchmark tests. FeatureBench, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (max thinking), %Passed / #Resolved / $ per task for Lite | Fast | Full: OpenHands 60.0/6/0.15 | 41.4/10/0.13 | 37.1/18/0.11; Claude Code (with DeepSeek backbone) 59.8/6/0.11 | 47.0/14/0.12 | 41.1/23/0.10; Mini-SWE-Agent 62.6/7/0.09 | 49.6/24/0.09 | 43.4/25/0.09; RTADev 65.3/6/0.17 | 49.7/15/0.16 | 46.1/26/0.15; CodeSpec 70.7/9/0.18 | 55.0/17/0.19 | 49.9/28/0.16. FeatureBench Lite, GPT-5.4-mini (medium thinking): Mini-SWE-Agent 47.5/2/0.7; OpenHands 48.1/3/1.2; RTADev 45.9/3/1.3; Codex 51.7/4/0.7; CodeSpec 54.7/5/1.3. Ablations (Lite, DeepSeek): w/o all specs 62.6/7/0.09; w/o behaviour spec 64.0/6/0.13; w/o architecture spec 66.6/7/0.16; w/o evidence 64.8/6/0.16; CodeSpec (Text) 43.8% vs CodeSpec 71.8% on 3,000-5,000-word instructions, ~51% vs 65.2% beyond 200 turns. NL2Repo, DeepSeek, overall %Passed/#Resolved/$: OpenHands 26.4/2/0.10; Claude Code 41.6/5/0.11; Mini-SWE-Agent 35.5/4/0.08; RTADev 41.3/7/0.14; CodeSpec 46.6/8/0.17 (Easy 70.0, Medium 51.7, Hard 20.4). Verdicts: CodeSpec quality partly (best %Passed everywhere, but at most ~71% of tests and few tasks fully resolved), cost works ($0.16-0.19 DeepSeek, $1.3 GPT-5.4-mini); baselines quality partly/does not work (OpenHands on NL2Repo), cost works

Tasks: FeatureBench Lite/Fast/Full (30/100/200), NL2Repo-Bench (104). Configurations: 5 scaffolds + CodeSpec; ablations and CodeSpec (Text) on Lite. Baseline: OpenHands, Mini-SWE-Agent, Claude Code, Codex, RTADev. Held constant: backbone DeepSeek-V4-Pro for all except Codex (GPT-5.4-mini); same repository environments, evaluation scripts and interaction budgets. Acceptance tests: benchmark fail-to-pass tests. Repetitions: Not stated (one run; bootstrap over tasks). Human intervention: none

CodeSpec best %Passed on all splits: +5.4 (Lite), +5.3 (Fast), +3.8 (Full) points over RTADev, at +$0.01-0.03 per task; with GPT-5.4-mini 54.7% vs Codex 51.7%; NL2Repo 46.6% vs Claude Code 41.6%. Ablations: removing all specs -8.1 points, behaviour spec -6.7, architecture spec -4.1, evidence -5.9. Executable vs textual specs: similar on short tasks, gaps widen on long instructions and >200 turns. Significance: no tests; bootstrap SDs (e.g., Lite ±5-6) overlap

Distinguished configurations on %Passed, though differences are within bootstrap SDs on small splits (Lite n=30). Repeatability: not assessed (single run). Limitations of the comparison: not stated by the authors
No limitations section. Stated in passing: smaller gain on Hard NL2Repo tasks reflects difficulty of coordinating larger requirements for current agents; specification steps add moderate cost
